title: row06
live_proof: inspection plus measurement in the 3.22.0 tree. The defect is in fts3EvalNextRow, but in its AND/NEAR branch at ext/fts3/fts3.c:5177 (pExpr->bEof = (pLeft->bEof || pRight->bEof)), not in the OR branch at :5216 -- the case recorded fts3.c:5134, which is the function's own declaration line, and called it the nested-OR branch. Settled 2026-10-16 by applying becd68ba0d's one line, pRight->bEof = pLeft->bEof = 1, to each candidate branch of the pinned amalgamation: after the AND/NEAR branch the use-after-free is gone AND the query still returns upstream's expected snippet one; after the OR branch the report is also gone but the query matches nothing (rows=0), which masks the defect rather than fixing it. Fixed upstream in 3.32.0
object: the Fts3SegReader allocation the snippet scorer's saved pHead/pTail point into (sqlite3Fts3SegReaderNew; 208 bytes on the host, a larger block on Capstone, where capability pointers widen the struct)
lifetime_ender: fts3EvalNextRow's AND/NEAR branch marks the node EOF as soon as one side is exhausted and leaves the other side with bEof==0 at a live docid, so fts3EvalTestExpr still counts it as a hit at the current row and fts3BestSnippet saves pointers into its reader; a later phrase's poslist fetch then restarts the group, and the reload (fts3EvalPhraseStart -> fts3EvalPhraseLoad -> fts3TermSelect) frees that reader
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3_PARENTHESIS, which is why this case has its own build group: without it the parentheses are ordinary characters, a flat query runs, and the case passes having tested nothing

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

status: re-measured 2026-10-16 on this platform: host ASan reports the heap-use-after-free (180 bytes inside a 208-byte region, fts3SnippetAdvance at sqlite3.c:164924); virtual-malloc MISSED with both controls as declared; virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 in fts3SnippetAdvance attributed by function, both controls as declared; cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping. Both of the case's own reachability checks passed in every run (snippet one and offsets 0 1 0 3 0 3 0 3). The arms block below is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
fault_sites_why: host ASan on the corrected trigger (results/2026-10-11-host-asan) reports the heap-use-after-free in fts3SnippetAdvance <- fts3SnippetNextCandidate <- fts3BestSnippet. Declared 2026-10-11, before the first Sublet run of that trigger.
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16 on the rebuilt platform; every recorded verdict holds and only the mechanism's location is corrected (see live_proof and PROVENANCE.md). Probe site 46 marks the save in fts3SnippetFindPositions, the free in sqlite3Fts3SegReaderFree and the read in fts3SnippetAdvance, printing the pointer at each: on native memsys5 the saved pointer is the reader's base+180 and that is what is read back (witness kind=UAF off=180), on virtual Capstone and on CheriBSD purecap it is base+268, the offset differing because capability pointers widen Fts3SegReader. The witness fires on all three, so unlike cases 07 and 08 this block is not reissued before the stale read. On CheriBSD the probe also prints tag=1 cb=<arena>+262144: the pointer is tagged and its bounds are the whole 256 KiB memsys5 arena, so the access is in bounds and the block's free is invisible to revocation -- the direct measurement of why that arm is silent, which cases 03, 05 and 06 established for this allocator. The three physical rows in results/matrix.tsv predate the 2026-10-11 trigger replacement and are marked superseded
